whiterhino_c: A very young rhinoceros calf standing on four legs in side view, only a few months old, with unmistakably infant proportions: an OVERSIZED HEAD too big for its body, SHORT STUBBY LEGS, a small rounded barrel body, a soft rounded forehead and big soft eyes. ON TOP OF ITS NOSE SITS ONE SMALL SOFT ROUNDED GREY KNOB, a low blunt bump about the size of its own eye, smooth and pebble-shaped and barely raised above the skin, sitting flat on the snout like a small river stone resting on a table - this little pebble-bump is the only thing on its nose and it is tiny, rounded and stubby, never tall, never pointed, never a spike. Below it a wide flat square grazing lip. Pale warm grey skin, LIGHT ALL OVER LIKE WET CEMENT, evenly and softly lit with no dark patches and no heavy shadows. Small round ears with tufted rims, a stubby tail
blackrhino_c: A very young rhinoceros calf seen from a THREE-QUARTER FRONT ANGLE, its head turned toward the viewer and its body angled away so both the face and one full flank show. Only a few months old, with unmistakably infant proportions: an OVERSIZED HEAD too big for its body, SHORT STUBBY LEGS, a small rounded body, a soft rounded forehead and big soft eyes. ON TOP OF ITS NOSE SITS ONE SMALL SOFT ROUNDED GREY KNOB, a low blunt bump about the size of its own eye, smooth and pebble-shaped and barely raised above the skin, like a small river stone resting on a table - this little pebble-bump is the only thing on its nose and it is tiny, rounded and stubby, never tall, never pointed, never a spike. Below it a POINTED HOOKED PREHENSILE UPPER LIP for browsing. Soft mid-grey skin, evenly lit, small tubular ears, a stubby tail
baskingshark: An enormous gentle plankton-straining sea creature drifting slowly with its jaws opened to their fullest extent, seen in side profile. Its open jaws form a VAST HOLLOW CIRCULAR RING as wide and as tall as its entire head, an open barrel mouth. THE ENTIRE INNER RIM OF THAT RING IS LINED WITH A DENSE SOFT FRINGE OF FINE PALE HAIR-LIKE BRISTLES, hundreds of them, packed close together like the bristles of a chimney brush or the teeth of a comb or a curtain of pale straw - a soft feathery fringe of thin flexible hairs is the only thing anywhere around that rim, soft and bendy and uniform, never hard, never sharp, never pointed, never triangular. Behind the ring, FIVE COLOSSAL GILL SLITS encircle the head almost completely, meeting over the top of the back and again beneath the throat, wrapping it in five deep grooves like stacked collars. A short blunt conical nose above the ring, a small dark eye, a bulky heavy grey-brown body, a tall triangular fin on its back, a crescent tail. Slow, harmless and gentle, straining water for tiny plankton
sunfishmola: A giant mola, an ocean creature that looks like AN ENORMOUS FLAT ROUND SILVER PLATE STANDING ON EDGE. ITS OUTLINE IS A CIRCLE - a full moon, a dinner plate, a car wheel - exactly as tall from back to belly as it is long from face to rear, squashed flat from side to side like a coin. THE REAR OF THIS DISC IS COMPLETELY MISSING, as though the whole back half of the creature had been SLICED CLEAN OFF WITH A KNIFE straight down: the body simply ENDS in a blunt vertical cut edge trimmed with a short WAVY SCALLOPED FRILL OF SKIN, a low ruffle lying flush against that cut like a pie crust or a lettuce edge, no longer than a hand. From the top of the circle ONE ENORMOUS POINTED FIN rises straight up and from the bottom an identical one points straight down, each nearly as long as the disc is wide, so the whole creature makes a tall vertical cross. A tiny round mouth, one large round eye, small pectoral fins, rough mottled silver-grey hide
oarfish: AN EXTREMELY LONG SILVER RIBBON-FISH SEEN IN STRICT FLAT SIDE PROFILE, its entire length turned broadside to the viewer so the full silhouette from head to tip lies flat across the picture, hanging vertically in deep water and drifting in slow S-shaped waves. THE PROPORTIONS ARE THE POINT: its body is a NARROW FLAT STRAP no deeper than a hand's width, running on and on for the whole height of the picture, at least TWENTY TIMES LONGER THAN IT IS DEEP, like a length of belt or a strip of foil unrolled. The strap TAPERS AWAY SMOOTHLY TO A FINE THREAD at its lower end and simply stops. A crimson fin of short rays runs the whole length of its back like piping along a seam. A TALL CREST OF LONG RED PLUMES rises from the top of its small blunt head, and two long red oar-shaped fins trail from just behind it. Silvery skin flecked with dark spots, one large dark eye
